title: Retinal tissue preparation for high-resolution live imaging of photoreceptors expressing multiple transgenes
author: Haeri, Zhuo, et al.

steps.title: Prepare imaging chamber
steps.instruction: Fill the imaging chamber with frog Ringer solution and place a clean coverslip at the bottom.

steps.title: Select healthy retinal tissues
steps.instruction: Scan the chamber and locate 10–15 healthy retinal tissue pieces that are well‑oriented and within 50 μm of the coverslip; prefer side‑on orientation (photoreceptor long axis parallel to the coverslip) and ensure photoreceptors are 10–20 μm from the coverslip at both ends for optimal imaging.

substeps.instruction: Identify side‑on or end‑on orientation; side‑on is preferred.
Confirm the tissue is thin‑cut with few broken or damaged photoreceptors.
Verify imaging depth will be ≤50 μm from the coverslip.

steps.title: Acquire live confocal images
steps.instruction: Using a confocal microscope, image the selected tissues while they remain bathed in frog Ringer solution; render surfaces with AxioVision 4.8 if needed, and include a 5 μm scale bar for reference.

substeps.instruction: Visualize any fluorescent tags present (e.g., soluble eGFP, eGFP‑arrestin, mCherry‑rhodopsin, eGFP‑mitochondrial, eGFP‑P23H, double‑geranylated eGFP).
Maintain imaging depth within 50 μm of the coverslip.

steps.title: Perform FRAP on live photoreceptor
steps.instruction: Select a single photoreceptor expressing double‑geranylated eGFP (eGFP‑dGryGry), bleach it with the FRAP laser, then record time‑lapse images for at least 50 seconds to assess fluorescence recovery.

substeps.instruction: Acquire live images immediately after bleaching and continue for ≥50 s.
Observe substantial lateral recovery after 50 s and minimal axial recovery.
